title: New Poll Says Morena Has 35% Support for 2027. PAN, 11; PRI, 9; MC, 9
author: SinEmbargo Editorial Staff
content:
_This article by the editorial staff of SinEmbargo originally appeared in
the[September 7, 2026 edition of
SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4866320/buendia-y-marquez-morena-
tiene-35-de-preferencia-para-2027-pan-11-pri-9-mc-9/), a Mexican digital news
outlet._

**Mexico City, September 7 (SinEmbargo).—** Just days before the start of the
2026-2027 electoral process, Morena maintains a wide lead heading into the
federal deputies election, while the opposition does not have a defined second
place, reveals the recent national in-home survey by Buendía & Márquez,
exclusively for El Universal.

The consulting firm details that, if the elections were held today, Morena
would concentrate **35 percent of electoral preference** , followed by the
National Action Party (PAN) with 11 percent. Meanwhile, the Institutional
Revolutionary Party (PRI) and Movimiento Ciudadano (MC) would each obtain nine
percent. The Ecologist Green Party of Mexico (PVEM) would reach five percent
and the Labor Party (PT), two percent.

![Raw voter preference bar chart](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/2026-09-07-buendia-marquez-morena-poll-chart-
raw.jpg)Raw voter preference: Morena 35%, PAN 11%, PRI 9%, MC 9%, Green Party
5%, PT 2%, Somos 1%, PAZ 0%, no answer 28%. Source: Buendía & Márquez / El
Universal.

The Buendía & Márquez survey notes that 28 percent of those consulted did not
state an electoral preference, so that, removing that proportion, the guinda
bench reaches **48 percent of the effective preference**. The PAN stands at 15
percent; the PRI, at 13 percent; and MC, at 12 percent.

![Effective preference trend line chart, February 2025 to August
2026](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/2026-09-07-buendia-marquez-morena-poll-chart-
effective.jpg)Effective preference (excluding non-responses), February
2025–August 2026: Morena 48%, PAN 15%, MC 13%, PRI 12%, Green Party 7%, PT 3%.
Source: Buendía & Márquez / El Universal.

It is important to note that, although the PAN has the highest estimate among
the opposition, the Mexican consultancy warns that its lead over the PRI and
MC is not wide enough to determine with statistical certainty which party
occupies second place. Nonetheless, it appears recurrently in the Buendía &
Márquez series of measurements, which points to a small but consistent
advantage over its competitors.

On the other hand, the newly created parties still show an incipient electoral
presence. According to the firm's figures, PAZ registered no mentions in the
sample; while Somos had just one percent.

According to Buendía & Márquez, the electorate is divided regarding the
country's direction, since 41 percent of those consulted consider that Mexico
is on a good or very good path, while **43 percent think it is on a bad or
very bad path**.

However, that discontent has not so far concentrated on a single opposition
alternative. Thus, according to the figures recorded by the consultancy, the
PAN obtains 27 percent of the effective preference among those who consider
that Mexico is on the wrong path, followed by the PRI and MC, which capture 19
percent each. Morena, for its part, retains 22 percent of the effective
preference among those who have a negative perception of the country's
direction.

![President Claudia Sheinbaum takes selfies with supporters at a Morena
rally](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/2026-09-07-buendia-marquez-morena-poll-
rally.jpg)Photo: Cuartoscuro

Despite this, the guinda party continues as the best-rated political force,
with 56 percent positive opinions and 29 percent negative opinions,
representing a favorable balance of 27 points.

Movimiento Ciudadano registers a positive balance of six points and the PVEM
of three, while the PT is practically in neutral territory, at minus one. In
contrast, the PAN and PRI hold the largest negative balances, at minus 27 and
minus 39 points, respectively, Buendía & Márquez explains.

The pollster also asked those consulted about some of the issues that have
occupied the recent public agenda. On that front, 78 percent said they had
heard news related to gasoline smuggling, or "fiscal huachicol," making this
the topic with the highest level of awareness among those included in the
measurement.

![Chart of public awareness of agenda topics](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/09/2026-09-07-buendia-marquez-morena-poll-chart-
agenda.jpg)Have you heard about…? Share who have heard each issue: "fiscal
huachicol" 78%, the request to detain Sinaloa governor Rocha Moya 62%,
limiting minors' social-media use 61%, the visa withdrawal of López Beltrán
50%. Source: Buendía & Márquez / El Universal.

In addition, 62 percent are aware of the request by the Southern District of
New York Prosecutor's Office to detain the governor of Sinaloa on leave, Rubén
Rocha Moya. Meanwhile, 61 percent have heard about the proposal to limit the
use of digital platforms and social media among children and adolescents; and
50 percent are aware of the withdrawal of the visa of Andrés López Beltrán,
son of former president Andrés Manuel López Obrador (AMLO), by the US
government.

However, Buendía & Márquez warns that awareness of these events does not
necessarily imply a change in electoral preferences. One example is the
perception of the withdrawal of visas from Mexican politicians, on which
public opinion is practically divided.

According to the figures gathered by the consultancy, 46 percent of those
surveyed believe that withdrawing a visa is a decision by the United States
(US) to determine who enters its territory, while 45 percent interpret it as a
form of political intervention in Mexico.

The different stances do show variations in electoral preferences, although
they do not substantially change the parties' positions. Thus, among those who
consider that the withdrawal of visas is a US decision, Morena obtains 41
percent of the effective preference, against 16 percent for the PAN, 16
percent for MC, and 13 percent for the PRI.

In contrast, among those who interpret the withdrawal of visas as a form of
political intervention, Morena reaches 53 percent; the PAN obtains 15 percent;
the PRI, 12 percent; and MC, 11 percent, says Buendía & Márquez.

With these results, the survey outlines a competition in which Morena retains
a wide advantage for the upcoming elections, while the opposition faces the
fragmentation of its preferences as one of its main challenges.
